leads.title: Wolf v. Walker - U.S. District Court for the Western District of Wisconsin
leads.documents: Struck down Wisconsin's constitutional and legislative ban on same-sex marriage as violation of Fourteenth Amendment; stay lifted after U.S. Supreme Court declined appeal, legalizing same-sex marriage Oct 6, 2014
leads.detail: Cited as Judge Barbara Brandriff Crabb ruling June 6, 2014; halted until Oct 6, 2014 citing Herbert; U.S. Supreme Court refused appeal in October

leads.title: Appling v. Walker (orig. Appling v. Doyle) - Wisconsin Supreme Court
leads.documents: Upheld constitutionality of Wisconsin domestic partnership registry Chapter 770 providing 43 spousal rights to same-sex couples
leads.detail: Cited as unanimous ruling July 31, 2014; registry established 2009 by biennial budget bill signed by Gov. Jim Doyle; ended April 1, 2018

leads.title: 1982 Wisconsin anti-discrimination law - first statewide sexual orientation protections
leads.documents: Bans discrimination based on sexual orientation in employment, housing, education, credit and public accommodations; no statewide gender identity protection
leads.detail: Cited as signed by Republican Governor Lee S. Dreyfus in 1982 with quote on government not intruding in private lives; Wisconsin first state to do so

leads.title: Governor Tony Evers Executive Order #1 - January 2019
leads.documents: Prohibits discrimination on basis of gender identity in government employment, issued in coordination with Fair Wisconsin
leads.detail: Cited as Executive Order #1, January 2019; contrasted with lack of state-level gender identity anti-discrimination law; only Dane/Milwaukee counties and cities Appleton, Cudahy, De Pere, Janesville, Madison, Milwaukee, Racine ban gender identity discrimination

leads.title: Wisconsin hate crime law
leads.documents: Punishes hate crimes based on sexual orientation as protected class, but does not include gender identity; perceived sexual orientation often used to prosecute anti-trans crimes
leads.detail: Cited in Hate crime law section: sexual orientation protected, gender identity not explicitly included

leads.title: Fields v. Smith - U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit
leads.documents: Ruled unanimous that 2005 Wisconsin Inmate Sex Change Prevention Act denying hormone therapy to prisoners undergoing sex reassignment is unconstitutional; prisoners entitled to hormone therapy
leads.detail: Cited as three-judge panel Aug 5, 2011; U.S. Supreme Court declined state appeal March 26, 2012; also notes sex offender registrants cannot change names with no transgender exception

leads.title: Wisconsin Legislature transgender medical care and sports bans 2021-2024 and Governor vetoes
leads.documents: Documents enforcement machinery for trans visitors: 2023 bill banning Medicaid coverage of sex reassignment/gender-affirming care, Oct 12-17 2023 youth gender-affirming care ban, and 2024 female sports/athletics ban - all vetoed by Gov. Evers
leads.detail: Cited as extensive budget bill June 2023 vetoed via line-item veto; Oct 2023 Evers statement to LGBTQ folks especially trans kids; Dec 6 2023 veto of under-18 ban; 2024 sports ban vetoed; May 2019 federal judge ordered Medicaid inclusion for non-government employees

leads.title: Milwaukee Police Department policy - September 2023
leads.documents: No longer lists gender (as well as race) of victims to avoid misgendering transgender individuals
leads.detail: Cited as Since September 2023 policy change

leads.title: Wisconsin Supreme Court July 2025 conversion therapy ruling and June 2021 executive order
leads.documents: Rules 4-3 that conversion therapy bans can be enacted by regulation and executive order bypassing legislature; 2021 order bans state taxpayer dollars funding conversion therapy on LGBT minors; 14 communities ban it
leads.detail: Cited as July 2025 4-3 ruling; June 2021 pride month executive order by Gov. Evers; Milwaukee March 2018 ordinance signed April 4 by Mayor Tom Barrett, Madison July 2018, Eau Claire Oct 2018 plus Cudahy, Shorewood, Racine, Glendale, Sheboygan, Superior, West Allis, Kenosha, Sun Prairie, Appleton, La Crosse; Jan 2023 GOP blocked code of conduct violation

leads.documents: Institutional human-rights profile of LGBTQ legal status and rights machinery in Wisconsin
leads.detail: Listed under External links as Wisconsin's Equality Profile - via the Movement Advancement Project
